organizations.name: Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS)
organizations.description: A systematic management system for establishing, implementing, operating, monitoring, reviewing, maintaining and improving an organization’s use of Artificial Intelligence.
organizations.source_text: AIMS is a systematic approach for establishing, implementing, operating, monitoring, reviewing, maintaining and improving an organization’s use of Artificial Intelligence to achieve business objectives.

organizations.name: ISO/IEC 42001:2023
organizations.description: The standard that provides the foundation for certification audits and a common model for implementing and operating an AIMS.
organizations.source_text: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 is formally entitled, “ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Management system”

organizations.name: Top management
organizations.description: The group responsible for showing commitment to the AIMS and ensuring policy, objectives, resources, and continual improvement.
organizations.source_text: The top management of the organization shall show commitment to the AIMS by doing the following:

roles.name: AIMS Core Team
roles.description: The team responsible for driving AIMS improvement, maintaining AI policy and documentation, reporting performance, and performing risk assessments.
roles.source_text: The AIMS Core Team is responsible for the following functions: ►Driving continuous improvement of the AIMS function overall ►Documenting and maintaining AB-Consultants AI policy and supporting documentation ►Reporting the performance of the AIMS program against established objectives to the management ►Performing ongoing risk assessments on all in-scope AI systems

roles.name: Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
roles.description: A role referenced as responsible for governance, policy approval, and decisions on the adequacy of AI controls.
roles.source_text: Chief Technology Officer (CTO) is responsible for the following functions: ►Governing the maintenance of policies and standards ►Making decisions on whether to accept the adequacy and associated risks of controls for AI Systems

roles.name: CISO
roles.description: A role referenced as governing the AIMS program, approving AI policies, and reviewing AI risks and controls.
roles.source_text: CISO is responsible for the following functions: ►Governing the AIMS program and its effectiveness ►Reviewing and approving Artificial Intelligence policies ►Reviewing the AI risks associated with operations and determining the levels of AI controls that are appropriate to protect such operations and systems.

roles.name: Policy, Certification and Compliance (PCC) Audit Team
roles.description: The team responsible for interfacing with auditors, coordinating ISO audit activities, and compiling documentation for audits.
roles.source_text: The PCC audit team is responsible for the following functions: ►Interfacing with the external auditors and internal auditees and for coordinating and facilitating the ISO audit activities ►Compiling existing documentation and providing applicable AI contacts for audit where necessary

roles.name: Lead for Policy, Certification and Compliance (PCC)
roles.description: The role serving as the point of contact for AI policy, implementation, monitoring, and control evaluation.
roles.source_text: The Lead for PCC is responsible for the following functions: ►Overseeing AIMS Core Team’s functions including the development and ongoing support of the AIMS Program ►Serving as the point of contact for AI policy, implementation and monitoring ►Periodically testing and evaluating AI controls and ensure deficiencies are remediate appropriately

roles.name: AI System Owners
roles.description: The role responsible for ensuring users understand system requirements, restricting access, separating critical functions, and providing AI control measures.
roles.source_text: AI System Owners are responsible for the following functions: ►Ensuring that users understand AI system requirements, AI system rules and their responsibilities prior to them being granted system access ►Confirming that user’s access to system is restricted to the minimum necessary to perform their job ►Ensuring that responsibilities for critical functions are separated among different individuals and that a single individual cannot easily commit a fraudulent activity ►Providing the appropriate Artificial Intelligence control measures

roles.name: AIMS Owner(s)
roles.description: A role listed as relevant to AI governance and the AIMS.
roles.source_text: Chief Executive Officer (CEO) / Chief Operations Officer (COO) ... AIMS Owner(s)

interested_parties.name: Interested parties
interested_parties.description: Parties whose needs and expectations relevant to Artificial Intelligence must be understood for the AIMS.
interested_parties.source_text: Before starting the design and implementation of the framework for managing AI systems, it is also important to define the interested parties relevant to AIMS as well as their expectations relevant to Artificial Intelligence.

interested_parties.name: Customers
interested_parties.description: External interested parties whose expectations include protection of data and AI systems and compliance with applicable laws and regulations.
interested_parties.source_text: Customers External Proper protection of customer data and AI systems demonstrated by being in control of Artificial Intelligence ... Compliance with the applicable laws and regulations.

interested_parties.name: Regulators
interested_parties.description: External interested parties whose expectations include compliance with applicable laws and regulations and responses to investigations and enquiries.
interested_parties.source_text: Regulators, Government and Authorities External Compliance with the applicable (Security, AI, Privacy) laws and regulations. Adopt an approach to update, meet and maintain these requirements. Prompt responses to investigations and enquiries.

interested_parties.name: Shareholders
interested_parties.description: Interested parties whose expectations include maintaining company profits through safe and responsible use of AI.
interested_parties.source_text: Investors and shareholders Internal / External Company profits are being maintained by ensuring safe and responsible use of AI.

interested_parties.name: Employees and contractors
interested_parties.description: Internal interested parties who need clear instructions, AI awareness, and protection of employee data.
interested_parties.source_text: Employees and contractors situated globally Internal Clear instructions on Artificial Intelligence and what is expected from them. Providing AI awareness sessions and protection of employee data.

interested_parties.name: Suppliers
interested_parties.description: External interested parties involved in contractual arrangements and secure integration of applications or systems.
interested_parties.source_text: Application vendors External Clear Artificial Intelligence requirements in the contractual arrangements. Secure integration of applications/systems according to contracts and relevant AI policies.

ai_systems.name: AI system
ai_systems.description: A machine-based system that infers from input how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions.
ai_systems.source_text: “An AI system is a machine-based system that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers from the input it receives how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments.

ai_systems.name: Generative AI
ai_systems.description: A type of artificial intelligence that can create new content such as images, text, audio, or video based on training data.
ai_systems.source_text: Generative AI is a type of artificial intelligence that can create new content such as images, text, audio, or video based on the data it has been trained on

ai_systems.name: Machine Learning
ai_systems.description: A subfield of artificial intelligence described as the capability of a machine to imitate intelligent human behaviour.
ai_systems.source_text: Machine Learning is a subfield of artificial intelligence, which is broadly defined as the capability of a machine to imitate intelligent human behaviour.

ai_systems.name: Deep Learning
ai_systems.description: A subset of machine learning defined as a neural network with three or more layers.
ai_systems.source_text: Deep learning is a subset of machine learning, which is essentially a neural network with three or more layers.

assets.name: AI and AI related assets
assets.description: Artificial intelligence resources and related assets that require protection and management.
assets.source_text: Protection of AI and AI related assets and prevention of ► Unauthorized access ► Data/Algorithmic Modification ► Inconsistent output of data/actions ► Breach of private user data ► Use for unintended purposes ► Legal Noncompliance

assets.name: Information assets
assets.description: Information assets requiring protection of confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
assets.source_text: Protection of confidentiality, integrity and availability of information and information assets.

assets.name: Customer data
assets.description: An example of information valued by the organization and subject to risk management.
assets.source_text: Customer data, operational procedures, records, etc.

assets.name: Operational procedures
assets.description: Organizational procedures identified as valued assets.
assets.source_text: Customer data, operational procedures, records, etc.

assets.name: Records
assets.description: Organizational records identified as valued assets.
assets.source_text: Customer data, operational procedures, records, etc.

assets.name: Hardware
assets.description: Physical technology assets such as servers, routers, and firewalls.

assets.name: People
assets.description: Human resources identified as assets valued by the organization.
assets.source_text: People Management, Development team, employees, etc.

assets.name: Location
assets.description: Physical locations such as data centers and offices identified as assets.
assets.source_text: Location Data center locations, offices, etc.

technologies.name: Large Language Models (LLM)
technologies.description: A technology category referenced as part of AI development and use.

technologies.name: Computer Vision
technologies.description: AI technology for processing, analyzing, and interpreting visual data.
technologies.source_text: Computer Vision Programs that help computers process, analyze, and interpret visual data (e.g., digital images or video)

technologies.name: transformer neural networks
technologies.description: A technique cited as enabling generative AI to create new content.
technologies.source_text: using techniques like large language models, transformer neural networks, and generative adversarial networks

business_processes.name: risk management process
business_processes.description: The process for establishing context, assessing, treating, accepting, monitoring, and communicating AI risk.
business_processes.source_text: The risk management lifecycle outlines the steps for effective management of the Artificial Intelligence risk management process: establish the context, risk assessment, risk treatment, risk acceptance, risk monitoring and risk communication

business_processes.name: Operational planning and control
business_processes.description: The process for planning, implementing, and controlling AI operations including outsourced relationships.
business_processes.source_text: Clause 8 — Operation covers operational planning and control, including Artificial Intelligence risk assessment and Artificial Intelligence risk treatment

business_processes.name: Management review
business_processes.description: A planned process to assess the AIMS for continuing suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness.
business_processes.source_text: Management review shall be conducted at planned intervals to ensure its continuing: Suitability Adequacy Effectiveness

business_processes.name: Internal audit programme
business_processes.description: The overall framework for a set of planned audits directed toward specific purposes.
business_processes.source_text: An audit programme describes the overall framework for a set of audits, planned for specific time frames and directed towards specific purposes.

business_processes.name: Corrective action process
business_processes.description: A process used to address nonconformities through documented corrective actions and root cause analysis.
business_processes.source_text: Corrective actions must be documented using the nonconformity report if a nonconformity is raised during the audit and processed electronically.

lifecycle_stages.name: Development
lifecycle_stages.description: A stage of the AI lifecycle referenced in control objectives and risk discussions.
lifecycle_stages.source_text: development, deployment, operation, change management, maintenance, transfer and decommissioning

lifecycle_stages.name: Deployment
lifecycle_stages.description: A stage in the AI system lifecycle requiring documented deployment plans and pre-deployment requirements.
lifecycle_stages.source_text: The organization shall document a deployment plan and ensure that appropriate requirements are met prior to deployment.

lifecycle_stages.name: Operation
lifecycle_stages.description: A stage in the AI system lifecycle covering ongoing use, monitoring, repairs, updates, and support.
lifecycle_stages.source_text: The organization shall define and document the necessary elements for the ongoing operation of the AI system.

lifecycle_stages.name: Monitoring
lifecycle_stages.description: A lifecycle stage where AI systems are observed for performance, drift, and related risks.

risks.name: AI risk
risks.description: Risk arising from AI systems that must be assessed, treated, accepted, monitored, and communicated.
risks.source_text: AIMS is based upon a risk assessment and the organization’s risk acceptance levels designed to effectively treat and manage risks.

risks.name: Risk appetite
risks.description: The level of risk an organization is willing to accept.
risks.source_text: The basic objective in establishing the context of risk management is to know the risk appetite, or the level of risk that an organization is willing to accept.

risks.name: Risk acceptance criteria
risks.description: Criteria defining which risks are acceptable and which require treatment.
risks.source_text: The level of risk that is acceptable should also be defined

risks.name: Risk treatment plan
risks.description: A plan for implementing selected controls and actions to reduce risks to acceptable levels.
risks.source_text: The risk treatment plan should consider the following factors and once formulated should be: ➢Aligned to the objectives of the organization ➢Available as documented information ➢Communicated within the organization

threats.name: Cyber attacks
threats.description: Malicious use of AI that can increase the volume and impact of attacks.
threats.source_text: Malicious AI use will “almost certainly” drive an increase in the volume and impact of cyber-attacks over the next two years, especially ransomware

threats.name: Deepfakes
threats.description: AI-generated content that can be used to defame or spread false information.
threats.source_text: Attackers can use AI for creating deepfakes and misinformation campaigns to defame or spread false information about individuals.

threats.name: Misinformation campaigns
threats.description: The use of AI to spread false or misleading information.
threats.source_text: Attackers can use AI for creating deepfakes and misinformation campaigns to defame or spread false information about individuals.

threats.name: Fraud
threats.description: AI-enabled malicious activity identified as a cybercrime risk.
threats.source_text: AI can be exploited for malicious purposes like cyber attacks, creating complicated malware and fraud.

threats.name: Autonomous weapons
threats.description: A destructive misuse of AI noted as an extreme harm scenario.
threats.source_text: It could be used for creating deadly autonomous weapons or facilitating cybercrimes.

vulnerabilities.name: Lack of transparency and explainability
vulnerabilities.description: A risk source that can reduce understanding of AI behavior and decisions.

vulnerabilities.name: Weak access control mechanisms
vulnerabilities.description: A vulnerability example involving inadequate access control.

vulnerabilities.name: Lack of logging/monitoring of unauthorized changes/activities
vulnerabilities.description: A vulnerability example involving insufficient logging and monitoring.
vulnerabilities.source_text: Lack of logging/monitoring of unauthorized changes/activities

vulnerabilities.name: Lack of segregation of duties
vulnerabilities.description: A vulnerability example involving insufficient separation of duties.

vulnerabilities.name: Inadequate data governance
vulnerabilities.description: A risk factor identified in the AI risk universe.

controls.name: Annex A (normative) Reference control objectives and controls
controls.description: The normative set of AI control objectives and controls used for risk treatment in ISO/IEC 42001:2023.
controls.source_text: Annex A (normative) Reference control objectives and controls

controls.name: Statement of Applicability
controls.description: A mandatory document stating applicable control objectives and controls and the reasons for inclusion or exclusion.
controls.source_text: Statement of Applicability is a mandatory document specifying the controls, reasons for inclusion or exclusion of the controls.

controls.name: AI policy
controls.description: A documented policy for the development or use of AI systems.
controls.source_text: The organization shall document a policy for the development or use of AI systems

controls.name: AI roles and responsibilities
controls.description: Roles and responsibilities for AI that must be defined and allocated according to organizational needs.
controls.source_text: Roles and responsibilities for AI shall be defined and allocated according to the needs of the organization.

controls.name: Reporting of concerns
controls.description: A process to report concerns about the organization’s role with respect to an AI system throughout its life cycle.
controls.source_text: The organization shall define and put in place a process to report concerns about the organization’s role with respect to an AI system throughout its life cycle.

controls.name: Resource documentation
controls.description: A control requiring documentation of relevant resources needed for AI lifecycle activities.
controls.source_text: The organization shall identify and document relevant resources required for the activities at given AI system life cycle stages and other AI-related activities relevant for the organization.

controls.name: AI system impact assessment process
controls.description: A process to assess potential consequences for individuals, groups, and societies throughout the AI system life cycle.
controls.source_text: The organization shall establish a process to assess the potential consequences for individuals or groups of individuals, or both, and societies that can result from the AI system throughout its life cycle.

controls.name: AI system verification and validation
controls.description: Defined and documented verification and validation measures and criteria for AI systems.
controls.source_text: The organization shall define and document verification and validation measures for the AI system and specify criteria for their use

controls.name: Data provenance
controls.description: A process for recording the provenance of data used in AI systems over the lifecycle of the data and AI system.
controls.source_text: The organization should define and document a process for recording the provenance of data used in its AI systems over the life cycles of the data and the AI system.

controls.name: Communication of incidents
controls.description: A plan for communicating incidents to users of the AI system.
controls.source_text: The organization shall determine and document a plan for communicating incidents to users of the AI system.

controls.name: Processes for responsible use of AI systems
controls.description: Documented processes for the responsible use of AI systems.
controls.source_text: The organization shall define and document the processes for the responsible use of AI systems.

controls.name: Intended use of the AI system
controls.description: A requirement to use the AI system according to its intended uses and accompanying documentation.
controls.source_text: The organization shall ensure that the AI system is used according to the intended uses of the AI system and its accompanying documentation.

policies.name: Artificial Intelligence policy
policies.description: The organization’s AI policy that is available as documented information, communicated, and aligned to objectives and requirements.
policies.source_text: The organization shall ensure that the AIMS policy is: ►available as documented information ►communicated within the organization ►available to interested parties, as appropriate

policies.name: Code of conduct
policies.description: A high-level policy referenced as part of the policy framework for AI.
policies.source_text: High-level general policies: • Code of conduct

policies.name: Integrated Management System Policies
policies.description: High-level policies referenced as part of the policy framework for AI.
policies.source_text: High-level general policies: • Integrated Management System Policies

policies.name: AI Data policy
policies.description: A topic-specific policy referenced under the AI policy framework.

policies.name: AI input requirements
policies.description: A topic-specific policy or requirement area referenced under the AI policy framework.

procedures.name: Data preparation
procedures.description: A defined method for selecting and preparing data for AI systems.
procedures.source_text: The organization shall define and document its criteria for selecting data preparations and the data preparation methods to be used.

procedures.name: AI risk assessment process
procedures.description: The documented process for assessing AI risks.

procedures.name: Risk treatment process
procedures.description: The documented process for treating AI risks.

procedures.name: Communication plan
procedures.description: The documented plan for communication relevant to the AIMS.

procedures.name: Operational planning and control
procedures.description: The documented operational control process for the AIMS.

standards.name: ISO 19011
standards.description: The guideline standard referenced for conducting internal audits in detail.
standards.source_text: Guidelines on how to perform an internal audit in detail can be found in the ISO 19011.

standards.name: ISO 9001
standards.description: An example management system standard cited in the course.
standards.source_text: Examples of management system standards: Quality Management Systems (QMS) ISO 9001

standards.name: ISO/IEC 27001
standards.description: An example management system standard cited as an information security management system standard.

legal_requirements.name: AI Act
legal_requirements.description: The proposed EU regulation that categorizes AI systems by risk level and applies to providers and users.
legal_requirements.source_text: The AI Act, proposed by the European Commission, aims to regulate AI use in the EU, applying to providers and users both within the EU and in third countries whose outputs affect the Union.

legal_requirements.name: Applicable legal requirements
legal_requirements.description: Legal requirements relevant to AI use, including prohibited use of AI.
legal_requirements.source_text: Applicable Legal requirements, including prohibited use of AI

legal_requirements.name: Copyright law
legal_requirements.description: A legal area implicated by AI training data and generated outputs.
legal_requirements.source_text: AI has been trained on copyrighted information.

legal_requirements.name: Data privacy regulations
legal_requirements.description: Legal requirements governing privacy and data use in AI contexts.
legal_requirements.source_text: This involves securing ample knowledge about legal limitations, data privacy regulations, and other law-driven stipulations, ensuring full compliance

objectives.name: AI objectives
objectives.description: Objectives for AI at relevant functions and levels that must align with the AI policy and be monitored and updated.
objectives.source_text: The organization shall define Artificial Intelligence objectives at relevant functions and levels.

objectives.name: AI governance and objectives
objectives.description: A lesson topic emphasizing governance objectives for AI management.

objectives.name: Continual improvement
objectives.description: The ongoing improvement of the AIMS's suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness.
objectives.source_text: the standard requires the organization shall continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the Artificial Intelligence Management System.

objectives.name: Responsible development objectives
objectives.description: Objectives that guide the responsible development of AI systems.
objectives.source_text: The organization shall identify and document objectives to guide the responsible development AI systems

objectives.name: Responsible use objectives
objectives.description: Objectives that guide the responsible use of AI systems.
objectives.source_text: The organization shall identify and document objectives to guide the responsible use of AI systems.

resources.description: Resources required to implement and sustain the AIMS, including human, financial, technical, documentation, and communication resources.
resources.source_text: Clause 7.1 - Resources ►Human resources ►Financial resources ►Technical resources ►Documentation resources ►Communication resources

resources.source_text: Control Ref A.4.6 Human resources Control Objective As part of resource identification, the organization shall document information about the human resources and their competences

resources.source_text: An AIMS needs financial resources, personnel with adequate training or experience, suitable facilities, and technical infrastructure

audits.description: Audits for which ISO/IEC 42001:2023 serves as the foundation.
audits.source_text: Its purpose is to serve as the foundation for certification audits

audits.name: Internal audits
audits.description: Planned audits used to determine conformity, implementation, and maintenance of the AIMS.
audits.source_text: The organization shall conduct internal audits at planned intervals to determine whether the control objectives, controls, processes and procedures of its AIMS:

monitoring_activities.name: Monitoring, Measurement, Analysis and Evaluation
monitoring_activities.description: The AIMS activity for evaluating AI performance and AIMS effectiveness.

monitoring_activities.name: Risk monitoring
monitoring_activities.description: Continuous monitoring of risks to detect changes in context and maintain an overview of the risk picture.
monitoring_activities.source_text: Risk monitoring is important for detecting any changes in the context of the organization, and to maintain an overview of the complete risk management process.

monitoring_activities.name: AI system operation and monitoring
monitoring_activities.description: Ongoing monitoring of AI system operation, performance, repairs, updates, and support.
monitoring_activities.source_text: The organization shall define and document the necessary elements for the ongoing operation of the AI system. At the minimum, this should include system and performance monitoring, repairs, updates and support.
